name: Jamarcus Johnson
strengths: Johnson's listed 6-5 / 330 looks real on sophomore Hudl — thick through the trunk, length to stack, and enough mass to force double teams at the point.
Johnson occupies doubles and clogs the A/B gap instead of getting washed — early tape shows he can keep linebackers clean when he wins with hands and leverage.
Johnson generates pocket push when he strikes first — drives the interior OL into the backfield and still shows enough lateral chase for a 330-pound frame.
weaknesses: Johnson still plays high on some snaps and needs cleaner, more violent hand placement — pad level and strike timing are the next polish items versus SEC interior OL.
comparison: Johnson comps to Dexter Lawrence — 6-4 / 6-5 massive interior mold; occupies doubles, pushes the pocket with mass, and still moves enough laterally to chase (size-matched; not a Florida-alum default).
projection: Johnson projects as develop into the Florida DL room with Year 1 rotation/nose-3T snaps, Year 2 compete for a starting interior role, with every-down starter upside as a space-eating, double-team magnet if pad level and hands catch the mass.
schemeFit: Johnson fits White's odd front as a nose/1-tech/3T who two-gaps, occupies doubles, and creates second-level clean-up with pocket push on early wins.

angle: Top-50 mass interior with Florida stake — Chatman/offer, 2 UOV, tape sell is occupy + push.
insiderNotes: Watched sophomore Hudl. Johnson wins with rare early mass at 6-5 / 330 — occupies doubles, pushes the pocket when he strikes, and still chases laterally. Pad level and hand violence need polish before every-down SEC claims lock.
